why: All three legs survive the challenge. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks.md (HTTP 200, 11740 bytes) puts the sentence on line 74, character-for-character, in the '## Missed runs' section. The whole line was read: the surrounding sentences reinforce rather than reverse it -- 'Desktop checks whether each task missed any runs in the last seven days', 'A daily task that missed six days runs once on wake', 'Desktop shows a notification when a catch-up run starts'. Line 70 of the same page ('If your computer sleeps through a scheduled time, the run is skipped') is about the in-session tick, not about the wake sweep, and the Missed-runs section is what governs. The page is row 97 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a real Claude Code contract page, not a Codex/MCP page conflated in. (2) CITED LINE: packages/shared/src/scheduler/scheduler-service.ts start() spans :33-45. :34 is the re-entrancy guard `if (this.timer || this.alignmentTimer) return;` and the described mechanism is at :37-44 -- `msUntilNextMinute` alignment, then `setInterval(() => this.tick(), 60_000)`. Off by a line or two on the anchor, dead accurate on the substance: there is no immediate tick, no replay, no persisted cursor; the first tick lands at the next minute boundary. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier: the durable Nessy analogue of Desktop scheduled tasks is the Automations subsystem (this repo says so itself at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:258 -- 'the DURABLE half of Claude's Desktop scheduled tasks mostly exists' in packages/shared/src/automations, with 'one catch-up run for the most recently missed time within seven days' named as part of the remaining gap, proposed as R31). Its scheduled trigger is packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:289 in matchesBasePredicate -- `return !!matcher.cron && matchesCron(matcher.cron, matcher.timezone)` -- and cron-matcher.ts:25-52 matches only whether the cron's nextRun falls inside the CURRENT minute window. No last-fired cursor is read anywhere on that path. Nothing upstream compensates: automation-system.ts:162 starts the scheduler and :396 only re-emits the tick onto the event bus; the history store (appendAutomationHistoryEntry, automations:getLastExecuted) is write-and-display only -- useAutomations.ts:62 hydrates lastExecutedAt purely for the 'last ran' label and no scheduling code reads it; retry-scheduler.ts is a webhook retry queue, unrelated; and grep -ain for powerMonitor over apps/electron/src/main and packages/server-core/src finds no OS wake/resume hook at all. So a daily 9am automation on a machine that was off at 9am does not run that day. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) -- and not a branding, subscription-flow or gateway product difference either. It is a recorded-but-OPEN product-surface gap, which is still a gap. TWO CORRECTIONS the finding needs, neither of which overturns it. First, the sibling-subsystem check does bite the wording: 'No catch-up of any kind' is overstated repo-wide, because packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts + cron-store.ts + packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts DO carry a lastFiredAt cursor, a cursorFor() helper and explicit catch-up prose (cron-scheduler.ts:121-131, cron-store.ts:198, sessions/index.ts:207). That tier delivers exactly one fire for an occurrence missed while the turn was busy and discards older ones because the cursor moves at delivery, not at enqueue (session-cron-service.ts:144-184). But that is the session-scoped Cron*//loop tier implementing scheduled-tasks.md:215, a DIFFERENT contract that forbids per-interval catch-up -- and session-cron-service.ts:9-16 explicitly documents why it is not SchedulerService. It is not the Desktop-Routines durable scheduler and does not survive an app restart in that sense, so it does not supply the behaviour this page specifies. Second, the finding's grep is scoped to only packages/shared/src/automations and packages/shared/src/scheduler; 'zero non-test hits' is true for those two directories but is not a repo-wide absence claim, and stating it as one is exactly how the sibling-subsystem trap fires. With the wording narrowed to the Automations subsystem, the divergence stands.
correctedState: Nessy's durable analogue of Desktop scheduled tasks is the Automations subsystem, and it performs no catch-up for occurrences missed while the app was closed or the machine asleep. SchedulerService.start() (packages/shared/src/scheduler/scheduler-service.ts:33-45) aligns to the next minute boundary and then ticks every 60_000 ms with no immediate tick and no replay; the scheduled-trigger predicate (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:289 -> cron-matcher.ts:25) asks only whether the cron matches the CURRENT minute and reads no last-fired cursor; automation history (appendAutomationHistoryEntry / automations:getLastExecuted) is display-only and never consulted for scheduling; and there is no powerMonitor wake hook anywhere in apps/electron/src/main or packages/server-core/src. A daily 9am automation on a machine that was off at 9am does not run that day, and no notification is shown. This is a recorded-but-open gap, not a decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:258 already names 'one catch-up run for the most recently missed time within seven days' as part of the Automations product-surface gap versus desktop-scheduled-tasks.md, proposed as R31. Separately -- and this is the part the original finding's grep scope hid -- a DIFFERENT subsystem does implement a single-fire catch-up: the session-scoped Cron tier (packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts, cron-store.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts) keeps a lastFiredAt cursor, delivers exactly one fire for a missed occurrence and discards older ones by moving the cursor at delivery rather than at enqueue. That tier implements scheduled-tasks.md:215 (the /loop contract, which forbids per-interval catch-up) and is deliberately not SchedulerService, per the rationale at session-cron-service.ts:9-16. So the accurate statement is 'the Automations scheduler has no catch-up', not 'no catch-up of any kind'.
